articles.originalTitle: Switzerland’s Fondation Beyeler opens £109.7m expansion - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Fondation Beyeler in Basel Opens £109.7m Expansion Project
articles.excerpt: Fondation Beyeler in Basel is expanding its exhibition space with three new structures designed by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor and an enlarged park area, operating with limited visitor numbers during its initial period.
articles.content: The Fondation Beyeler in Basel, Switzerland, is opening its expanded facilities following a project costing approximately SFr 120m. Home to Modern art collections including works by Claude Monet, Piet Mondrian, and Pablo Picasso, the institution has increased its internal space with three new structures designed by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor, alongside regenerated grounds. Funded largely by Swiss entrepreneur Hansjörg Wyss, the primary new gallery building increases exhibition space by 1,500 sq. m. The freestanding Ammann Pavilion provides a venue for recitals and performances, while the Erlen Torhaus adds office space to the property's 18th-century villa. Furthermore, the surrounding parkland has doubled to nearly 20,000 sq. m, featuring installations by Rachel Whiteread, Pierre Huyghe, and Louise Bourgeois. Eschewing a traditional large inauguration party, museum director Sam Keller announced a controlled opening period from 26 September to 27 January 2027 with limited visitor numbers to optimize operations. Concurrently, a new exhibition titled Constellations presents 150 modern and contemporary works until 5 September 2027, bridging the original Renzo Piano galleries with Zumthor's new spaces.

articles.originalTitle: K-art, William Kentridge and a Turner prize worth getting excited for – the week in art - The Guardian
articles.title: Turner Prize Exhibition Opens in Middlesbrough Alongside Global Art Events
articles.excerpt: The 2026 Turner Prize exhibition opens at MIMA in Middlesbrough, while the British Museum in London launches a major survey spanning 2,000 years of Korean art.
articles.content: The MIMA gallery in Middlesbrough is hosting the 2026 Turner Prize exhibition, running from 26 September until 29 March. The showcase features Kira Freije, who constructs a wasteland populated by Rodinesque figures, alongside works by Simeon Barclay exploring masculinity and Tanoa Sasraku addressing big oil. In London, the British Museum opens a survey spanning 2,000 years of Korean art, belief, and philosophy from 1 October until 31 January. Meanwhile, the Paul Stolper Gallery presents Mark Wallinger's paintings and a film examining abstraction and the vitality of nature until 24 October, and the Goodman Gallery hosts the world premiere of William Kentridge's new animated film until 7 November. At the National Gallery, Rembrandt's portrayal of Saint Paul draws attention for its raw depiction of human suffering and doubt. Separately, the Greek Prime Minister stated that an agreement regarding the return of the Parthenon marbles could still be reached.

articles.originalTitle: The astonishing story of Van Gogh collector Gertrud Dübi-Müller is finally celebrated in an exhibition at Switzerland’s Kunstmuseum Basel - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Art Collector Gertrud Dübi-Müller's Life Celebrated at Kunstmuseum Basel
articles.excerpt: Kunstmuseum Basel is hosting an exhibition celebrating the life and pioneering art collecting of Gertrud Dübi-Müller, who purchased a Van Gogh portrait as a teenager in 1908.
articles.content: The life and collecting journey of Swiss pioneer Gertrud Dübi-Müller are the focus of an exhibition at the Kunstmuseum Basel. Inheriting wealth from her family's engineering business after being orphaned at a young age, Müller acquired Vincent van Gogh's Portrait of Charles-Elzéard Trabuc in 1908 when she was only 19 years old. This purchase predated widespread international recognition for the artist and sparked considerable enthusiasm among her avant-garde circle, including artists Cuno Amiet and Giovanni Giacometti. Alongside her early art acquisitions, Müller led an adventurous life, becoming the first woman in Solothurn to own a car. She later married lawyer Otto Dübi in 1921 and maintained her dedication to modern art throughout her life. Upon her death in 1980, Dübi-Müller bequeathed 190 works to the Kunstmuseum Solothurn, including pieces by Paul Cezanne, Henri Matisse, and Pablo Picasso alongside works by her Swiss artist friends. The exhibition runs until 7 February 2027, highlighting her remarkable early acquisition and her enduring engagement with modern art.

articles.originalTitle: Glenn Brown in: Fail We May, Sail We Must | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Brown Collection Opens Fail We May, Sail We Must Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Curated by Glenn Brown and Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition brings together historic and contemporary works at the Brown Collection. The event showcases paintings, sculptures, drawings, and ceramics by more than twenty artists.
articles.content: The Brown Collection in London is hosting a new exhibition on view from September 25, 2026, to August 7, 2027. Titled Fail We May, Sail We Must, the exhibition was curated by Glenn Brown and his husband, Brown Collection cofounder Edgar Laguinia. The presentation aims to challenge mental mechanisms through art spanning six centuries, creating new connections between works that are rarely seen together. The selection features paintings, sculptures, drawings, prints, and ceramics by more than twenty artists, including spliced collages, double images, and elongated figures. Work created by Brown is also included in the exhibition. Infused with playfulness and humor, the project invites viewers to examine relationships formed across different historical periods. Visitors can access the exhibition at the London location during the specified dates.

articles.originalTitle: Ai Weiwei unveils his epic new Australian work: ‘90% of art is just garbage. Real art questions the existing order’ - The Guardian
articles.title: Ai Weiwei Unveils 40-Meter Combat Helmet Sculpture Installation in Sydney
articles.excerpt: Residing on his Portuguese farm, artist Ai Weiwei has unveiled Mushrooms, a 40-meter installation featuring 500 identical cast iron combat helmet sculptures outside Sydney's Museum of Contemporary Art.
articles.content: Residing on his secluded farm in the Portuguese countryside, acclaimed artist Ai Weiwei has introduced his latest creation, Mushrooms, on display outside Sydney's Museum of Contemporary Art on the Tallawoladah Lawn. Serving as this year's Neil Balnaves Tallawoladah Lawn Commission, the monumental installation stretches 40 meters in length and comprises 500 identical cast iron sculptures shaped like combat helmets on an elevated platform. The title references the visual link between mushroom caps and helmets, alongside fungal associations with decay, death, and the fragility of life laid bare by armed conflict. The artist explained that the origins of the commission trace back to 2015 during the production of his migrant crisis documentary, Human Flow, which prompted him to study military arsenals and warfare mechanics. He noted that Germany's initial offer of helmets to Ukraine at the onset of the conflict influenced his perspective. Having visited frontline Ukrainian soldiers multiple times last year, Ai argued that art must question the existing order rather than merely serve decorative or sentimental purposes. He contended that contemporary art institutions frequently favor pleasant works over those addressing human struggle and reality. Mushrooms is free to visit on the Tallawoladah Lawn at the Museum of Contemporary Art in Sydney.

articles.originalTitle: Major Retrospective of Sri Lankan Architect Geoffrey Bawa Opens at the Vitra Design Museum - Architectural Record
articles.title: Major Geoffrey Bawa Retrospective Opens at the Vitra Design Museum in Germany
articles.excerpt: A comprehensive retrospective examining the five-decade career of influential Sri Lankan architect Geoffrey Bawa has opened at the Vitra Design Museum in Germany.
articles.content: A major retrospective on Sri Lankan architect Geoffrey Bawa has opened at the Vitra Design Museum in Weil am Rhein, Germany. Titled Geoffrey Bawa: Architecture for the Senses, the exhibition examines the architect's five-decade career through more than 250 drawings, models, photographs, furniture pieces, and archival documents. Organized by the Vitra Design Museum, M+, and the Wüstenrot Foundation in collaboration with the Geoffrey Bawa Trust, the retrospective marks the first major display of his work in over two decades. The exhibition features material from projects such as the Kandalama Hotel and his country estate Lunuganga, accompanied by newly commissioned photographs by Iwan Baan that emphasize the relationship between the buildings and their surroundings. The curation also highlights Bawa's collaborations with local artists and craftspeople, integrating textiles and sculptures into the spatial experience. Designed by Lebanese architect Lina Ghotmeh, the exhibition remains on view in Germany until February 28, 2027, before traveling to M+ in Hong Kong in June 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Aziz Hazara SculptureCenter Show Is A Portrait of Life Under Sanctions - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Aziz Hazara Exhibition at SculptureCenter Examines Life Under Sanctions
articles.excerpt: Artist Aziz Hazara explores the logistics of empire and the remnants of the US withdrawal from Afghanistan in his exhibition titled "Coming Home" at SculptureCenter in New York.
articles.content: New York's SculptureCenter is hosting the exhibition "Coming Home" by artist Aziz Hazara, on view through December 28. The exhibition features discarded objects collected from Bagram Air Base following the United States' withdrawal from Afghanistan, including tea kettles, scanners, camouflage knee pads, and folded refugee housing tents. Following the abrupt US departure in August 2021 after two decades of military involvement, Afghanistan faced severe sanctions, halted foreign aid, and frozen assets. Speaking from his studio in Berlin, Hazara described the project as a portrait of life under sanctions and the complex supply chains left in the wake of war. After five years of navigating bureaucratic hurdles, shell companies, and sanctions, the artist successfully transported the materials to New York. The exhibition presents these physical remnants to offer a tangible perspective on militarized occupation and the logistical networks of imperial presence.

articles.originalTitle: Herzog & de Meuron reuses foundations for mass-timber Massachusetts school building - Dezeen
articles.title: Herzog & de Meuron Reuses Existing Foundations for Massachusetts College Building
articles.excerpt: Swiss architecture studio Herzog & de Meuron has utilised existing concrete foundations for a new Student Center and Dining Commons at Amherst College, incorporating mass-timber levels and deep solar-shading eaves.
articles.content: Swiss architecture studio Herzog & de Meuron has utilised the existing concrete foundation of an older structure for the Student Center and Dining Commons at Amherst College in Massachusetts, expanding the building from 80,000 to 120,000 square feet. Working alongside executive architect Sasaki, the studio preserved two lower-level foundations of the former Merrill Science Center to navigate the sloped site and align with the institution's carbon neutrality goals. Two upper levels constructed primarily from Canadian Black Spruce mass timber were added atop the skeleton, featuring light-oiled Western Red Cedar cladding above and dark-stained timber on the lower levels. The structural design connects mass-timber columns directly to pre-existing concrete supports using split-beam and corbel joints. The third level accommodates study and event spaces alongside a winter garden courtyard, while the roof holds low-lying pavilions containing a black-box theatre and solar panel arrays. According to the studio, the design achieves a 33 per cent reduction in embodied carbon and a 93 per cent reduction in operational carbon compared to conventional building types. This project marks Herzog & de Meuron's first completed educational building in the United States.

articles.originalTitle: Architectural Details: Snider House Bridges Past and Present - Architizer
articles.title: Giannone Petricone Associates Revitalizes 1828 Snider House in North Toronto
articles.excerpt: Giannone Petricone Associates has restored and updated Snider House, North Toronto's oldest surviving building, blending historic design with a glass addition.
articles.content: Giannone Petricone Associates has restored and revitalized Snider House, identified as the oldest surviving building in North Toronto. Originally built in 1828 in the Regency style, the landmark was upgraded to modern standards while preserving its historic character. The original Regency cottage façade maintains its formal, symmetrical presence at the front, while a contemporary rear glass extension opens the dwelling to the landscape. Co-founding principal Pina Petricone notes that the firm approaches heritage projects to celebrate distinct attributes through contrast and layering. The standout architectural feature at the rear is an undulating, two-story glass façade. Fabricated using a gravity-curved method on hot sand beds in Spain and combined with low-E insulated glass technology, this custom curtain wall contrasts with the heavy clay brick of the original structure. Inside, the restored interior balances heritage formality with material restraint, maintaining warmth in the dining and sitting rooms. The kitchen and adjoining living areas open fully to the backyard. Reimagined wide baseboards function simultaneously as visual accents and air diffusers, helping the historic home meet contemporary standards.

articles.originalTitle: Fondation Beyeler Expands with Three New Buildings by Peter Zumthor - ArchDaily
articles.title: Fondation Beyeler Expands with Three New Buildings by Peter Zumthor
articles.excerpt: The Fondation Beyeler in Riehen, Switzerland, is expanding its museum ensemble with three new buildings designed by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor.
articles.content: The Fondation Beyeler in Riehen, Switzerland, is expanding its museum ensemble with three new buildings by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor, an enlarged and restored park, and the adaptive reuse of several historic structures. The expansion extends the existing museum designed by Renzo Piano, adding exhibition, education, cultural, and public spaces while opening a previously private section of the surrounding landscape to visitors. Zumthor's additions comprise the Wyss Museum, the Ammann Pavilion, and the Erlen Torhaus, positioned within the existing landscape and differentiated through their programmes, forms, and material treatments. The largest addition, the three-storey Wyss Museum, adds approximately 1,500 square meters of exhibition space. Its Y-shaped plan is arranged around existing trees, including a ginkgo, a redwood, and a group of plane trees. Locally quarried Jura limestone is used throughout the building, including in the rammed-concrete façade, terrazzo flooring, staircases, benches, and wall finishes. Located between the two museum buildings and the historic structures, the Ammann Pavilion acts as a public gathering space with a single-storey glass and oak structure. The landscape expansion adds almost 10,000 square meters of formerly private parkland, nearly doubling the size of Beyeler Park and connecting it directly to the Landschaftspark Wiese nature reserve.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Exhibition Explores 1,600 Years of Art in Constantinople and Istanbul
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is preparing to host a major exhibition examining the artistic legacy of two successive empires from AD 330 to 1922.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum has announced the upcoming exhibition titled "Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires," opening on 7 November 2026. Hosted at V&A South Kensington, the exhibition explores 1,600 years of art, design, and architecture in the imperial capital from AD 330 to 1922. It examines the distinct yet connected traditions of the Byzantine and Ottoman empires across four main sections. Visitors will encounter more than 200 objects, including rarely seen textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, sculpture, manuscripts, and paintings. Structured around sections titled Grand Beginnings, Heaven and Earth, Power and Reach, and Life in the City, the display highlights the city's strategic infrastructure, sacred imagery, imperial court spectacles, and cosmopolitan urban life. The exhibition also traces the enduring influence of Byzantine and Ottoman art on 19th-century Europe through works drawn from the V&A collection.

articles.originalTitle: peter zumthor's expanded fondation beyeler opens to the public - Designboom
articles.title: Peter Zumthor's Expanded Fondation Beyeler Opens to the Public
articles.excerpt: Peter Zumthor’s expansion of the Fondation Beyeler in Riehen near Basel begins its opening to the public with new buildings and an expanded park.
articles.content: Peter Zumthor’s expansion of the Fondation Beyeler in Riehen near Basel begins its opening to the public, with the new ensemble gradually revealed from September 2026. Three new buildings, an expanded park, and restored historic structures extend the museum beyond Renzo Piano’s existing structure, creating a larger setting for art, architecture, nature, and public life. Following a study involving 11 architecture practices, Zumthor’s proposal was unanimously selected by the international jury, dividing the new functions between three buildings with distinct forms and materials to reduce overall volume. The Wyss Museum adds around 1,500 square meters of exhibition space across three floors using Jura limestone and rammed concrete. The Ammann Pavilion acts as a social center combining glass and oak, opening broadly onto the park for public use and evening cultural events. The architectural expansion is accompanied by the opening of almost 10,000 square meters of formerly private parkland to the public, extending 19th-century English landscape gardens. Several existing historic structures, including the Orangerie and Ammann Atelier, have also been restored and given new functions for education, botany, and art programmes.

articles.originalTitle: Google Unveils New Renderings of Chicago's Thompson Center Redesign, Marking Its Escape From Demolition - ArchDaily
articles.title: Chicago's Thompson Center Escapes Demolition with New Redesign Renderings
articles.excerpt: Chicago's postmodern James R. Thompson Center is being redeveloped as a space for work, culture, and community, escaping demolition through a collaboration with studio A+I.
articles.content: New redevelopment renderings have been released for the James R. Thompson Center in Chicago's Loop, designed by Helmut Jahn and completed in 1985. Commissioned by Governor James R. Thompson, the postmodern building features a multicolored glass atrium and a sloping corner entry. Facing criticism over maintenance costs and climate control issues, the structure was repeatedly threatened with demolition until preservationists campaigned for its protection. The building was sold to The Prime Group in 2022, and Google announced plans to purchase it following renovations. Renovations began in May 2024, involving the removal of portions of the original exterior and atrium. Developed in collaboration with Architecture Plus Information, now part of Perkins&Will, the redesign integrates food, retail, and seasonal event spaces into the 17-story atrium and plaza. The revamped public area will also house Vector, a 30-foot sculpture by artist Sanford Biggers, alongside a large-scale commissioned piece produced with the local nonprofit After School Matters.

articles.originalTitle: Standout Collectible Designs at Paris Design Week 2026 - WWD
articles.title: Standout Collectible Designs Unveiled During Paris Design Week
articles.excerpt: The 16th edition of Paris Design Week featured 500 exhibitors across showrooms in Saint-Germain-des-Prés and beyond, showcasing contemporary collectibles, lighting, and natural material furnishings rooted in traditional techniques.
articles.content: Paris Design Week marked its 16th edition with 500 exhibitors presenting contemporary decor and design across showrooms in Saint-Germain-des-Prés and other districts. Draga & Aurel presented their Crisalide side tables featuring fused colored glass and sand-cast brass bases at Galerie BSL. Interior firm Pinto and luxury textile house Nobilis revived their past partnership to present Foundation, a collection characterized by warm tones and jacquard motifs. Yves Salomon Éditions unveiled Tactile Monuments, its first complete interior collection inspired by stones and natural volumes, utilizing merino shearling. Swedish design house Veermakers opened an appointment-only showroom in Le Marais, while Nordic Knots exhibited wool rugs inspired by Swedish Grace. L’Objet partnered with diamond jeweler Jessica McCormack on a marine-themed home and tableware collection. Modern Metier presented Tropic of Capricorn, a seven-piece series created with French designer Rudy Guénaire. Garnier & Linker introduced Aurora, an outdoor lighting collection combining cast aluminum and alabaster. Franck Genser exhibited items including his Piscine VI coffee table, and Hervet Manufacturier displayed its woodworking collections drawing on historical expertise.

articles.originalTitle: Sansetsukon x Es Devlin: MILK - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Dance Collective Sansetsukon Performs New Live Work at V&A East Storehouse
articles.excerpt: Dance collective Sansetsukon is staging MILK, a new live performance responding to Es Devlin's installation The Everythingists, at the V&A East Storehouse.
articles.content: Dance collective Sansetsukon is presenting MILK, a new live performance responding to Es Devlin's installation The Everythingists through dance, sound, light, and shadow. Staged as a free special event on 3 October 2026 at the V&A East Storehouse, the performance creates a dialogue between the dancers, the installation, and the surrounding gallery space. The work draws inspiration from Rayonism and the concept of new art challenging old art, while also exploring ideas of humans empowered by machines and machines empowered by individuals. Set to an audio soundscape created by reworking material from The Everythingists, the 25 to 30-minute performance takes place across three sessions. The production features dancers including Joshua Shanny-Wynter, Deavion Brown, and Robbie Ordoña, alongside a creative team comprising composer Serian Griffiths and lighting designer Oliver Pritchard.

articles.originalTitle: 200,000 young people and counting: Tate celebrates a new generation with landmark commission for young artists - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Collective Reaches 200,000 Members and Launches Landmark Open Call
articles.excerpt: Tate Collective, the free membership scheme for 16 to 25-year-olds, has reached 200,000 members and launched an open call for a new artwork to be displayed at Tate Modern.
articles.content: Tate Collective, a free membership scheme for 16 to 25-year-olds, has reached a milestone of 200,000 members. To mark the occasion, an open call has been launched inviting members to create a new artwork for display at Tate Modern alongside figures such as Andy Warhol, Salvador Dalí, and Marina Abramović. The winning commission will be selected by a jury chaired by Rosalie Doubal and will go on display in March 2027, with submissions closing on 19 October. Concurrently, Tate Modern Lates is celebrating its 10th anniversary, having drawn 870,000 attendees over the past decade to after-hours events featuring live music, performances, and workshops. Karin Hindsbo, Interim Director of Tate, stated that the members represent a generation choosing to engage with art and ideas. The anniversary celebrations will culminate on 30 October with a special Late event programmed by Shygirl. Tate Collective membership offers various discounts and access to creative opportunities with support from patrons and foundations.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale College Architettura 2026/2027: the 12 selected projects - labiennale.org
articles.title: Twelve Projects Selected for Biennale College Architettura 2026-2027
articles.excerpt: Twelve projects have been selected for the third edition of Biennale College Architettura. The projects by practitioners under 30 will be developed during a workshop from 22 to 30 September 2026.
articles.content: Twelve projects have been selected for the 3rd edition of Biennale College Architettura 2026–2027. The emerging practitioners under 30 originate from China, Croatia, Italy, Mexico, Syria, Spain, Turkey, Tunisia, the USA, and Hungary. The initiative complements the 20th International Architecture Exhibition, titled Do Architecture and curated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu, serving as a research, experimentation, and production laboratory. The open call attracted over 80 emerging practitioners from 36 countries. The 12 selected projects are presented by Ahlem Balghouthi, Fabio Bari, Stav Bouzaglo, Antonino Caridi, Yiying Chen, Alejandro Ferrer Esplugues, Jin Gao, Nisa Gökgöz, Matej Orkić, Julia Polefko, Ahmad Salah, and Guillermo Sanchez Cardenas. The workshop will take place from 22 to 30 September 2026, coordinated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu alongside tutors. Following the workshop, up to four projects will be selected to receive a 25,000 euro grant for the realization of the final work, which will be presented out of competition during Biennale Architettura 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel Paris 2026 Press Dossier: a deep-dive into this year's highlights - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Paris 2026 Prepares with 211 Galleries and Expanded Sectors
articles.excerpt: The Art Basel Paris 2026 fair prepares to open its doors in October with 211 galleries from 41 countries and regions. The event features an expanded program, including the relocation of Premise to Salon Seine and numerous first-time participants.
articles.content: Art Basel Paris announced preparations for its 2026 edition featuring 211 galleries. The fair includes 183 galleries in the Galeries sector, 16 in Emergence, and 12 in Premise, representing 41 countries and regions. This year, the Premise sector moves to a larger space named Salon Seine, while Conversations relocates to the Grand Palais Auditorium and the new Square Jean Perrin entrance. There are 64 galleries operating in France, and France-based participants continue to play a central role across the sector. The event welcomes 32 first-time participants, with 9 making their debut in an Art Basel fair. Over 170 galleries are returning, alongside 6 galleries graduating from Emergence into the main sector and more than 30 galleries younger than 10 years old. The Avant-Première preview returns on October 20. The fair brings together leading Modern, post-war, and contemporary art dealers from France and beyond, featuring an expanded public program centered around multidisciplinary practices including painting, installation, performance, literature, dance, and moving image.

articles.originalTitle: Black Wall Street Journey: Re and De Imagining Black Progress: Rick Lowe | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Rick Lowe's Largest Institutional Solo Exhibition Opens in Michigan
articles.excerpt: Artist Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, Black Wall Street Journey, will run from September 26, 2026, to January 24, 2027, at the University of Michigan Museum of Art.
articles.content: Titled Black Wall Street Journey, the exhibition will run from September 26, 2026, to January 24, 2027, at the University of Michigan Museum of Art in Ann Arbor. This presentation marks Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States. Bringing together painting, sculpture, and public installation, the public art project examines how Black prosperity, resilience, and self-determination are represented, measured, and understood. The exhibition is the culmination of the artist's three-year residency at the University of Michigan's Institute for Social Research, reflecting engagement with researchers, data scientists, and students. By working collaboratively across art, data, and inquiry, the project examines the forces shaping Black wealth and opportunity, spanning income, education, housing, and business ownership.

articles.originalTitle: ARTIST ROOMS: Robert Rauschenberg at Tate Modern, 21 September 2026 - December 2027 – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern Opens Large-Scale Robert Rauschenberg Display
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free display of over 20 works by Robert Rauschenberg spanning three decades to mark the centenary of his birth.
articles.content: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free display of works by Robert Rauschenberg, running from 21 September 2026 to December 2027. Marking the centenary of the artist's birth, the presentation brings together over 20 works spanning three decades, including paintings, prints, and kinetic installations. At the heart of the presentation are Glut sculptures, including three newly gifted by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation to the Tate Americas Foundation. Curated by Gregor Muir, Andrew de Brún, and Julia Blaut, the display foregrounds Rauschenberg's engagement with dance and performance, featuring metal sculptures, performance sets, and costume designs. The exhibition is organized as part of the ARTIST ROOMS touring programme, jointly managed by Tate and the National Galleries of Scotland.

articles.originalTitle: Maison Michel Celebrates 90 Years of Hatmaking With New Exhibition at Chanel’s Le19M - WWD
articles.title: Parisian Hatmaker Maison Michel Celebrates 90th Anniversary With Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Paris-based hatmaker Maison Michel is celebrating its 90th anniversary with a dedicated exhibition at La Galerie du 19M, highlighting traditional craftsmanship techniques and historical workshop processes.
articles.content: Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel is launching a new exhibition at La Galerie du 19M to mark its 90th anniversary. Part of a craftsmanship network since 1997, the workshop focuses the display on ancient tools and techniques as much as final designs. Titled "Metamorphoses — The Hats of Maison Michel," the exhibition opens with raw materials carved from tree trunks alongside archived wooden hat blocks. Visitors can explore the detailed processes of milliners working with canvas, organza, leather, and tweed. Maison Michel remains one of the few producers mastering sewn straw techniques. The space also features specially commissioned artworks, runway designs, and historical haute couture creations. Curated by the atelier's artistic director and a museum director, the event captures the sonic ambiance of the workshop. The venue further includes a replica of an early 20th-century milliner's shop alongside weekly filmmaking workshops. Experts note that headgear has evolved from restrictive social conventions of the past into an individualized form of self-expression today.

articles.originalTitle: 6 artists to watch at the Lyon Biennale 2026 - Art Basel
articles.title: The 18th Lyon Biennale Explores Exchange and Transition Under Curator Catherine Nichols
articles.excerpt: Curated by Catherine Nichols, the 18th Lyon Biennale brings together 118 artists from around the world across several key venues from September through December 2026.
articles.content: Founded in 1991, the Lyon Biennale returns in September for its 18th edition across several key venues in the city. Curated by Australian writer and art historian Catherine Nichols, the ambitious program brings together 118 artists from around the world. Titled To Pass from One Dream to Another and inspired by Lyon's traboules, the biennale examines physical transitions between spaces and historical layers. Drawing on Robert Filliou's principles of poetic economy, Nichols organizes the event around three distinct layers: the existential at macLYON, the relational at the Musée des Tissus, and the industrial at Les Grandes Locos. The edition features a constellation of artists rarely shown in France, alongside a particularly strong presence from the Oceanian scene. Showcasing works by practitioners such as Akwasi Bediako Afrane, Hana Miletić, Serwah Attafuah, Luke Willis Thompson, Angela Goh, and Minh Lan Tran, the 18th Lyon Biennale runs from September 19 to December 13, 2026.
